target_customer: Agricultural operators and crop-protection service providers, plus logistics, humanitarian and defense customers
problem: Crop spraying by crewed aircraft is dangerous and costly, and remote cargo delivery lacks cheap aircraft. Pyka builds autonomous electric fixed-wing aircraft for both.
business_model: Hardware sales of aircraft through distributors plus autonomy software, with defense contracts
product_category: Autonomous electric aircraft (crop protection and cargo)

founders.name: Michael Norcia
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CEO on the YC page. No education listed there.

founders.name: Nathan White
founders.background_notes: YC page lists both Norcia and White as Founder/CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires building an autonomous electric aircraft with custom flight control, avionics, motors and batteries, plus aviation regulatory approval. Research-grade hardware for a new team in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: FAA authorization for a large uncrewed spray aircraft (reported 2023) and vertically integrated hardware and autonomy are hard to copy quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Yamaha uncrewed helicopters were already used for spraying in California per one Aviation Week mention, but no incumbent copied Pyka's electric fixed-wing approach in the sources found.

market_need_then: Aerial application is dangerous for pilots and electrification and autonomy were emerging. No dated 2017 evidence was opened, so this is partly inferred from the later product focus.

branding.domain_note: Uses flypyka.com, not the exact pyka.com, per the YC page.

identity.mascot_or_character: Product line named Pelican (Pelican Spray, Pelican Cargo, Pelican 2)
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and commercial press release voice

brand_strength.rationale: Brand mostly known through trade press about aircraft and funding. Pelican is a live trademark per an aggregator listing. No evidence of community or brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Autonomous electric aircraft focused on crop spraying
pivots.why: TechCrunch headline says Pyka adapted its aircraft for cargo runs with the Series A, per search results. Defense DropShip added in 2025.

outcome_analysis: Pyka raised a seed in 2019, a Series A in 2022 and a Series B in 2024, won FAA authorization for crop spraying in 2023 and began selling through distributors in Brazil and the US in 2025. It then added a defense cargo aircraft, DropShip. Hardware and certification make progress slow but build a moat.
notes: Total raised conflicts: ZoomInfo $88M, CB Insights $95M, versus $88M from the recorded rounds. Seed investors not seen in an opened source. Series B and A confirmed by company press releases and outlets. Founders have no education or prior employers on the YC page. Competitor list left empty: Yamaha and Hylio (founded 2015 per CB Insights) appear only in undated or later sources. DropShip USAF contract lacks official confirmation per one outlet.
